[[File:Corrosion icon.png|right]]
'''Corrosion''' is an [[Arts Reaction]] in ''[[Arknights: Endfield]]''.

==Overview==
===Friendly===
<span>'''Corrosion''', when applied to enemies, is a debuff that progressively reduces Resistance. Corrosion lasts for a specified duration and instantly reduces the Resistances against <span style="border-bottom: 1px dotted #fff;">{{Template:Tooltip|all elements|title= All elements|content=Elements include: {{Color|Physical|1}}, {{Color|Nature|5}}, {{Color|Cryo|4}}, {{Color|Electric|6}}, {{Color|Heat|3}} }}</span> of the target by a flat amount and further reduces it over time until a certain minimum. In-game, the Resistance of enemies is rated by letters, starting with 'D' for 0 Resistance, resulting in no reduction for incoming damage; 'C' usually means about 20 Resistance (20% damage reduction or a 0.8 multiplier), and so on.</span>

It is important to note that the Resistance value can be reduced below 0, meaning that Corrosion does work even against enemies that have a Resistance of 0. 

Because of the additive behavior, the effects of Corrosion are more effective on enemies with a higher Resistance:
* Against an enemy with 0 Resistance, reducing it by 24 (to a total of -24 Resistance) results in 24% increased damage taken or a 1.24 multiplier.
* A [[Heavy Ram]] has 20 Resistance for incoming Physical Damage, subtracting the 24 points decreases the Resistance value from 20 to -4, turning the 20% reduction into a 4% increase of Physical Damage taken, or in other words, increases the incoming damage multiplier from 0.8 to 1.04, effectively increasing the damage taken by 30% in contrast to the 24% from the first example.

When a {{G|Nature Infliction}} is applied to an enemy with a ([[File:Heat Infliction icon.png|16x16px|link=]]/[[File:Electric Infliction icon.png|16x16px|link=]]/[[File:Cryo Infliction icon.png|16x16px|link=]]) Non-Nature Infliction, the Arts Infliction that was applied first is {{G|Debuff Consumption|consumed}} instead to trigger {{G|Corrosion}}.
* The debuff lasts for {{Color|15|1d}}s (unless otherwise specified).
* Deals an initial instance of {{Color|160% – 400% of ATK (based on the Status Level)|1d}} as {{Color|Nature DMG|5}}.
* Applies a Resistance Reduction of {{Color|3.6 – 7.2|1d}} on application that increases by {{Color|0.84 – 1.68|1d}} each second until it reaches {{Color|12 – 24 (based on Status Level)|1d}}.

! {{G|Status Level}} !! Initial Nature DMG !! Initial Resistance Reduction !! Resistance Reduction Increase Over Time !! Max Resistance Reduction

|-

|}

*[[Arts Intensity]] increases the amplitude of the Resistance Reduction.
* It is possible to reduce the Resistance of an enemy below zero through Corrosion, causing them to take increased damage.
* Applying Corrosion to a target with an existing Corrosion causes the new Corrosion's Resistance Reduction to be equal to the old Corrosion's Resistance Reduction if it was higher.
** This may cause the new Corrosion to have a Resistance Reduction value that is over its Max Resistance Reduction, in which case the new Corrosion's Resistance Reduction value will be equal to the higher of the two and won't be further increased.
* Some operator skills can also {{Tooltip/Forcibly apply|Arts|forcibly apply}} Corrosion without requiring a different Arts Infliction to be {{G|Debuff Consumption|consumed}} (See [[Arts Reaction]] for more information).

===Hostile===
{{Quote|Certain enemy skills can apply stacks of Nature Infliction to operators. At 4 stacks, the operator becomes Corroded: Cannot dash and suffer movement speed reduction for a certain duration.|Tutorial}}
As of [[Dreamscape of Wind and Snow]] version, there are no enemies capable of applying Corrosion.

==Calculations==
===Initial Nature DMG hit===
{{Main|Damage calculation}}

===Resistance Reduction===

<math>{Resistance\,Multiplier} = \dfrac{100 - Enemy\,Resistance + Ignore\,Resistance + Final\,Corrosion\,Resistance\,Reduction}{100} </math>

<math>{Final\,Corrosion\,Resistance\,Reduction} = {Corrosion\,Resistance\,Reduction} \times {Arts\,Intensity\,Multiplier}</math>

Each point of [[Arts Intensity]] increases the effect by some percent, decreasing with more points of Arts Intensity up to a soft cap of {{Color|300%|1d}}.

<math>{Arts\,Intensity\,Multiplier} = \dfrac{3 \times Arts\,Intensity + 300}{Arts\,Intensity + 300}</math><br>
{| class="wikitable wikitable-mobile"
|-
! Arts Intensity !! Arts Intensity Multiplier
|-
| 0 || 100%
|-
| 100 || 150%
|-
| 200 || 180%
|-
| 300 || 200%
|-
| 400 || 214%
|-
| 500 || 225%
|}
